(frog-substitute)=
# frog-substitute

<!-- Generated by generate_readme.py from the CLI definitions in src/frogchem/cli. Do not edit by hand. -->

{bdg-secondary}`Substitution` Substitute atoms of molecules with fragments, keeping the scaffold fixed.

## What it does

Building a series of derivatives by hand in a viewer (replace this H by Cl, Br, OMe, CF3, ...)
is slow and gives uneven starting geometries. This command does it automatically: it removes
an atom of your molecule, attaches a substituent from a built-in library (or your own XYZ
fragment) in its place, rotates it to avoid clashes and relaxes **only the new fragment** with
a force field, leaving the rest of the molecule exactly where it was. Use it to prepare
substituent screens (e.g. all halogens, all aryls) on a catalyst or substrate before the QM
optimisations.

## How it works

```{include} _parts/frog-substitute/how_it_works.md
```

## Input

* The base molecule as an `.xyz` file, ideally already optimised.
* The target site as two 0-based atom numbers: the atom to **replace** (usually an H) and the
  atom it is bonded to (the **anchor**, which will carry the substituent). Look them up in a
  viewer (the first atom of the file is 0), or pick them with `--gui-pick`.
* A fragment name from the library (`frog-sub-db list`, e.g. `phenyl`, `methoxy`), a scope
  preset (`frog-sub-db scopes`, e.g. `halogens`), or your own fragment XYZ with `--frag`.
* The default relaxation uses the RDKit force field. `--method aimnet` (AIMNet2 machine-learned
  potential, installed with FROG) is closer to DFT and accepts charged systems (`--charge`), but
  covers main-group elements only (no transition metals);
  `--method mace` needs `pip install mace-torch`. `--method xtb` is **not implemented yet**.
  If a calculator cannot be started, a warning is printed and RDKit is used instead.

### Arguments

**Options**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--mol` `XYZ …` | required | Base molecule file(s) (XYZ) |
| `--combined-xyz` `PATH` |  | Also write all substituted molecules to this multi-structure XYZ |
| `--buffer` `Å` | `0.3` | Bonding buffer in Å for the topology check |
| `--clash` `Å` | `0.8` | Clash distance in Å used while rotating the fragment |
| `--rotations` `N` | `36` | Number of dihedral angles sampled for clash avoidance |
| `--track` `IDX …` |  | Original atom indices (0-based) to track: written to an 'original_id' column (extended XYZ), -1 for the other atoms |

**Fragment selection**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--db-frag` `NAME` |  | One fragment from the library, e.g. phenyl |
| `--db-frags` `NAME …` |  | Several fragments from the library, e.g. methyl ethyl isopropyl |
| `--scope` `SCOPE` |  | Scope preset, category, tag, comma-separated names or 'all' (e.g. halogens, alkyls, aryls, ewg, edg) |
| `--frag` `XYZ` |  | Custom fragment XYZ file (use with --frag-pair) |
| `--frag-pair` `DELETE ATTACH` |  | Fragment atoms (0-based): atom deleted on attachment and attachment atom |

**Target selection**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--mol-pairs` `IDX …` |  | Target sites as flat pairs of 0-based indices: REPLACE ANCHOR [REPLACE ANCHOR ...] |
| `--gui-pick` |  | Pick the target atom pairs in a 3D viewer |

**Optimization**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-opt` |  | Skip the relaxation (geometric placement only) |
| `--method` `{rdkit,aimnet,mace,xtb}` | `rdkit` | Method used to relax the fragment (xtb is not implemented yet: it falls back to the RDKit force field) |
| `--optimizer` `{lbfgs,fire,rdkit,backtracking}` | `lbfgs` | Optimizer used with ML calculators |
| `--no-freeze-core` |  | Let the scaffold atoms move during the relaxation |
| `--traj` |  | Write the optimization trajectory (.traj) |
| `--device` `DEVICE` | `cpu` | Device for ML calculators (cpu, cuda) |
| `--charge` `CHARGE` | `0` | Total charge of the system |

**Output**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--out-dir` `DIR` |  | Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input file) |

Shared by every command: `-v/--verbose`, `-q/--quiet`, `--format {table,json,csv}`, `--table-file PATH` — see [CLI conventions](conventions.md).

## Output

| Kind | Name | When | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Terminal | `Fragment Substitution Summary` | always | One row per molecule and fragment: status, core RMSD (Å), number of atoms, output file |
| File | `<stem>_<fragment>.xyz` | always | Substituted molecule; <fragment> is the library name, or the --frag file stem |
| File | `<stem>_<fragment>_opt.traj` | `--traj` | ASE optimization trajectory (ML calculators only) |
| File | `PATH` | `--combined-xyz` | All substituted molecules in one multi-structure XYZ |
| File | `frogchem/substituter/data/library.json` | `--frag` | Fragment library, updated in place when a new custom fragment is registered |

### How to read it

A *Fragment Substitution Summary* with one row per molecule and fragment: **Status**
(SUCCESS/FAILED), **Core RMSD** (how much the original atoms moved, Å), number of atoms and the
output file. Example: toluene + phenyl at atom 10/4 → SUCCESS, core RMSD 0.0000 Å, 25 atoms;
`--scope halogens` gives `tol_fluoro.xyz` … `tol_iodo.xyz`, 15 atoms each.

* Core RMSD is 0 by design (the scaffold is frozen); with `--no-freeze-core` it shows how much the
  scaffold relaxed.
* The geometry is a force-field guess, **not** a minimum: always reoptimise it with your QM method.
  With `--no-opt` the fragment is only placed geometrically.
* `Optimization incomplete` means the relaxation stopped early: inspect the structure for clashes.
* A custom fragment given with `--frag` is **added to the fragment library** (the package data
  file) unless an identical one is already there; remove it later with `frog-sub-db remove`.
* `--track 0 4` adds an `original_id` column (extended XYZ): the original index for the tracked
  atoms, -1 for all the others (including the fragment atoms).

## Step by step

1. Find the site: in `tol.xyz` (toluene) the para H is atom 10, bonded to the para carbon, atom 4.
2. Substitute: `frog-substitute --mol tol.xyz --mol-pairs 10 4 --db-frag phenyl --out-dir subs` writes `subs/tol_phenyl.xyz` (without `--out-dir` it is written next to the input).
3. Screen several fragments: `--db-frags methyl ethyl isopropyl` or `--scope halogens`; add `--combined-xyz subs/all.xyz` to get all derivatives in one file for quick viewing.
4. Several sites at once: give more pairs, `--mol-pairs 10 4 7 0` (each pair REPLACE ANCHOR).
5. Use your own fragment: `--frag OMe.xyz --frag-pair 4 0` (fragment atom 4 is the dummy/H that is removed, atom 0 is the atom that bonds to the molecule).
6. Open the result in a viewer and use it as the start of a normal QM optimisation.

## Full reference

Every option, as printed by `frog-substitute --help`:

:::{dropdown} `frog-substitute --help`
```text
usage: frog-substitute [-h] [-v] [-q] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--table-file PATH] --mol XYZ
                       [XYZ ...] [--combined-xyz PATH] [--out-dir DIR] [--db-frag NAME]
                       [--db-frags NAME [NAME ...]] [--scope SCOPE] [--frag XYZ]
                       [--frag-pair DELETE ATTACH] [--mol-pairs IDX [IDX ...]] [--gui-pick]
                       [--no-opt] [--method {rdkit,aimnet,mace,xtb}]
                       [--optimizer {lbfgs,fire,rdkit,backtracking}] [--no-freeze-core] [--traj]
                       [--device DEVICE] [--charge CHARGE] [--buffer Å] [--clash Å]
                       [--rotations N] [--track IDX [IDX ...]]

Substitute atoms of molecules with fragments, keeping the scaffold fixed.

Replaces atoms in base molecule(s) with functional fragments from the curated library (see frog-
sub-db), a scope preset or a custom XYZ file. Bond lengths are set from atomic radii, the fragment
is rotated to avoid clashes and then relaxed with the scaffold frozen (core RMSD 0 Å).

Target sites are pairs 'REPLACE ANCHOR' of 0-based atom indices of the base molecule: the REPLACE
atom is removed and the fragment is bonded to ANCHOR. A custom fragment (--frag) is registered in
the fragment library unless an identical one is already there.

options:
  -h, --help                    show this help message and exit
  --mol XYZ [XYZ ...]           Base molecule file(s) (XYZ)
  --combined-xyz PATH           Also write all substituted molecules to this multi-structure XYZ
  --buffer Å                    Bonding buffer in Å for the topology check (default: 0.3)
  --clash Å                     Clash distance in Å used while rotating the fragment (default:
                                0.8)
  --rotations N                 Number of dihedral angles sampled for clash avoidance (default:
                                36)
  --track IDX [IDX ...]         Original atom indices (0-based) to track: written to an
                                'original_id' column (extended XYZ), -1 for the other atoms

fragment selection:
  --db-frag NAME                One fragment from the library, e.g. phenyl
  --db-frags NAME [NAME ...]    Several fragments from the library, e.g. methyl ethyl isopropyl
  --scope SCOPE                 Scope preset, category, tag, comma-separated names or 'all' (e.g.
                                halogens, alkyls, aryls, ewg, edg)
  --frag XYZ                    Custom fragment XYZ file (use with --frag-pair)
  --frag-pair DELETE ATTACH     Fragment atoms (0-based): atom deleted on attachment and
                                attachment atom

target selection:
  --mol-pairs IDX [IDX ...]     Target sites as flat pairs of 0-based indices: REPLACE ANCHOR
                                [REPLACE ANCHOR ...]
  --gui-pick                    Pick the target atom pairs in a 3D viewer

optimization:
  --no-opt                      Skip the relaxation (geometric placement only)
  --method {rdkit,aimnet,mace,xtb}
                                Method used to relax the fragment (xtb is not implemented yet: it
                                falls back to the RDKit force field) (default: rdkit)
  --optimizer {lbfgs,fire,rdkit,backtracking}
                                Optimizer used with ML calculators (default: lbfgs)
  --no-freeze-core              Let the scaffold atoms move during the relaxation
  --traj                        Write the optimization trajectory (.traj)
  --device DEVICE               Device for ML calculators (cpu, cuda) (default: cpu)
  --charge CHARGE               Total charge of the system (default: 0)

output:
  -v, --verbose                 Enable debug output
  -q, --quiet                   Suppress banner, info and saved-file messages
  --format {table,json,csv}     Format of the tables printed on stdout (default: table)
  --table-file PATH             Also write all tables to PATH (.json, .csv or .txt; otherwise the
                                --format is used)
  --out-dir DIR                 Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input
                                file)

outputs:
  terminal (stdout; --format table|json|csv, --table-file PATH):
    Fragment Substitution Summary
                                One row per molecule and fragment: status, core RMSD (Å), number
                                of atoms, output file
  files (next to each input, or --out-dir):
    <stem>_<fragment>.xyz       Substituted molecule; <fragment> is the library name, or the
                                --frag file stem
    <stem>_<fragment>_opt.traj  [--traj] ASE optimization trajectory (ML calculators only)
    PATH                        [--combined-xyz] All substituted molecules in one multi-structure
                                XYZ
    frogchem/substituter/data/library.json
                                [--frag] Fragment library, updated in place when a new custom
                                fragment is registered

examples:
  frog-substitute --mol cat.xyz --mol-pairs 12 3 --db-frag phenyl
      Replace atom 12 (bonded to atom 3) with a phenyl group
  frog-substitute --mol cat.xyz --mol-pairs 12 3 --scope halogens --out-dir derivs --combined-xyz derivs/all.xyz
      Screen all halogens on one site; one file per derivative plus a combined XYZ
  frog-substitute --mol cat.xyz --mol-pairs 12 3 --frag OMe.xyz --frag-pair 4 0 --method aimnet
      Attach a custom fragment (delete atom 4, bond through atom 0) and relax it with
      AIMNet2

Data go to stdout, messages to stderr. Atom indices are 0-based unless stated otherwise.
Step-by-step guide (what it is for, what you need, what to expect): docs/cli/frog-substitute.md.
```
